Nioh 3's first DLC hits in August, brings new weapons, a trip to the (sort of) future, and there's a mega-hard difficulty mode for the sickos
summary: Are you sickos?
body: I will be truthful: if you grabbed me by the lapels and demanded I tell you when Nioh 3 came out, I would answer something along the lines of 'the late 1980s'. The fact that the third Nioh—a rather good game, per our 90% Nioh 3 review —only released in February of this year feels like a weft in the tapestry of space-time. But so it was, and so it is that Nioh 3 will, on August 19, get its first DLC in the form of Hell Rising : "Our protagonist and appointed shogun, Takechiyo, journeys through time and is led to Edo in the future by an unknown yokai he met in his dreams," goes the blurb. "Edo in the future" is the year 1651, by the by. Things aren't looking great. "The large castle town that was once proof of the shogunate’s authority has transformed into a hellish wasteland plagued by the gales of the Crucible," rumbles the DLC description. "Yokai, human rebels, and alchemists from foreign lands have descended on Edo, creating a battlefield fraught with chaos." I knew a guy in uni who called himself an alchemist from foreign lands, but he was just a Latvian guy who sold cannabis. The new DLC brings new gear with it. Hell Rising brings the hoko and shield and ninja hoko and shield.…

title: Alienware 34 AW3426DW review
summary: Alienware's updated 34-inch ultrawide OLED monitor is even more awesome than the original.
body: Can it really be well over four years since Alienware rolled out the AW3423DW , the first mainstream OLED gaming monitor? The AW3423DW wasn't perfect, but by many important gaming metrics, it absolutely monstered every LCD-based display. That model, of course, was a 34-inch ultrawide and now Alienware has released its most significant update yet for that form factor, the Alienware 34 AW3426DW . So, what does four years of OLED gaming monitor development buy you? In really simple terms, some new threads, a bit more brightness, and a higher refresh rate. But when you dig down into the details, there's way more going on here. Most importantly, Alienware has upgraded to Samsung's very latest QD-OLED panel tech, known as Penta Tandem. In terms of headline specs, that means a bump from 250 nits full-screen and 1,000 nits peak HDR brightness of that OG Alienware OLED, to 300 nits and 1,300 nits respectively. You also get an upgrade from VESA DisplayHDR 400 True Black to 500 True Black certification, again highlighting the punchier panel. title: You won't have to worry about limited bandwidth or data now that Valve has fixed  local network game transfers on Steam
summary: Sharing is caring—here's how to check your Steam client is up to date.
body: One saving grace of a flat mate is setting up 'family sharing' on each other's Steam libraries at the earliest opportunity. Another saving grace is leveraging local network game transfers to then have a go at whichever game has become your roommate's flavour of the month, and judging them accordingly. Recently though, Steam's local network game transfers hadn't been working as intended. For instance, some folk would attempt to kick off a local transfer, only for Steam to download via the internet instead. That's less than ideal if your bandwidth is scarce or you're working with limited data. Thankfully, Valve shipped a fix to the stable channel of the Steam Client on Monday. That means, you should now be able to transfer games between gaming desktops, laptops, and handhelds like the Steam Deck once more—so long as you've got the most up to date version of the Steam client installed. Stick with me, because I'll tell you how to check Steam is up to date on your PC and Steam Deck. To check you're up to date on PC, open the client, click 'Steam' in the top left corner, and click 'Check for Steam Client Updates…' from the drop down menu. title: Zach Cregger may have made the best Resident Evil movie yet, but a faction of fans aren't happy about it
summary: The latest reboot of the Resident Evil movie series is taking some heat for not looking Resident Evil-ey enough.
body: I'm in such a bubble of positivity for Barbarian and Weapons director Zach Cregger's upcoming Resident Evil movie (out September 18) that I had no idea anyone was upset about it until I looked at the reactions to some of PC Gamer's coverage. The movie is Resident Evil "in name and nothing else," one person wrote in reply to one of our social media posts. As it turns out, some Resident Evil fans are unhappy that the film doesn't directly adapt any of the games, that it takes liberties with the setting—there were no iPhones or snow-covered streets in Resident Evil 2—and that it 'doesn't look like Resident Evil.' It's true that the first trailer (embedded above) doesn't scream 'Resident Evil,' though I assume that's by design. Explicit references to the setting are withheld until after the title reveal, when we hear in the stinger that the protagonist's very bad day takes place in Raccoon City. Theater audiences are meant to go ooh and then connect the dots they missed earlier in the trailer, like the conspicuously-placed typewriter, a reference to Resident Evil's save locations. But this is obviously not a straight adaptation of Resident Evil 2. Rather than putting existing Resident…

title: 'Wtf is going on': Indie dev discovers their neglected Steam game is powering an Undertale multiplayer mod following its freak 1700% jump in player activity
summary: Little-known platformer Crashphalt is enjoying an unexpected popularity—but its players are enjoying something else.
body: A few months ago, indie developer RetroSpecter noticed something unusual about Crashphalt , their first completed game that launched on Steam in 2018: Since their last check-in on the neglected platformer, Crashphalt had suddenly gained over 500 reviews. In its first four years, it had barely managed a dozen. And almost none of those new reviewers had anything to say about Crashphalt itself. Mostly, they just talked about Undertale. (Image credit: Cold Pressed Games) "Does ANYONE want to play Undertale with me???" one reviewer writes. Another calls Crashphalt the "best game to never actually play." Others insist that "Undertale is a pretty cool game." "Okay yeah I like Undertale too," RetroSpecter wrote in a Reddit thread recounting their discovery, "but wtf is going on?" Crashphalt owed its unexpected renaissance, they soon realized, to Undertale Together , a fan-made Undertale multiplayer mod that, typically, only supports local co-op—a limitation that players found a clever way to circumvent. title: Cyan releases teaser for the first new Myst game in 20 years, then breaks the news that it's not actually being made
summary: Project Anglerfish looks great, but publishers apparently aren't interested.
body: Myst was a massive success: Not only was it the best-selling PC videogame of all time for years, it helped usher in the CD-ROM era, opening the door to expansive new technologies and previously unseen levels of fidelity in gaming. In 1993, Myst was nothing short of a revelation. The fortunes of Myst, and developer Cyan Worlds, have waned since then. The most recent game in the series, Myst 5: End of Ages, came out in 2005 and was reasonably well received but not a big seller; Cyan, after years of financial struggles, has moved onto Myst-like games including Firmament and Obduction, both of them reliant on crowdfunding. The studio laid off "roughly half" its staff in 2025, leading PC Gamer's Justin Wagner to write that "it's galling to see a historic indie like Cyan Worlds hit so hard" by the brutal, ongoing contraction of the game industry. Justin sure wasn't wrong about that, but some folks are finding this even more galling: Over the weekend Cyan released a teaser for a new Myst game, codenamed Project Anglerfish, which looks really good—and then said it's not in development because apparently publishers aren't interested. title: This cat-themed PC case has the best power button I've ever seen
summary: Simply the cat's pyjamas.
body: I've been watching Colorfire's cat-themed Meow product line with much interest over the years. While I've already got a kitty-eared headset , I'm sure a full feline-themed set-up would help me achieve my final form as a hardware writer. The Meow series' ME26A PC case may prove the perfect canvas towards realising that dream. In terms of styling, the ME26A is low-key compared to other entries in the Meow series. For starters, pizza-eating mascot Bobi is seemingly nowhere to be seen (unlike the Meow-X gaming PC set Colorfire showed off at last year's Computex ). There's a very fun 'Meow'-shaped air grate on the front, and even a bit of tasteful wooden trim. The cat hasn't completely left the build, though. The ME26A PC case also enjoys an almost subtle kitty paw motif, with orange decals on the chassis itself, just above the front I/O panel. Daubed in kitty pawprints, the front I/O features 1x USB-A, plus 1x USB-C port rated for up to 20 Gbps. It also happens to feature one of the best power buttons I've ever seen—if I can start my day by squishing fake toe beans, I know it's going to be a good day (via VideoCardz ). Honestly, I already can't imagine a better thing to play Cat Mail …

title: Framework 13 Pro review
summary: The best laptop Framework's ever produced, and one of the best I've ever used.
body: The moment you touch the new Framework 13 Pro laptop you know it's different to what's come before. Despite the bubblegum pink USB Type-C ports I've jammed in either side of the machine, this is a serious laptop for serious work. But it's also still instantly recognisable as one of the company's eminently upgradeable and repairable notebooks. This is the true beauty of Framework's new machine, a laptop that at once exists as the pinnacle of its hardware journey, but also steadfastly refuses to compromise on the core principles that has made it one of my favourite PC builders. Though, it must be said, that refusal to compromise here comes at a hell of a cost because of the focus on ultra expensive LPCAMM2 memory. This is a next-generation Framework laptop, but is still completely compatible with every Framework 13 device the company has shipped in the past five years or so. That is a hell of an achievement, meaning that you could have an ageing 13-inch laptop and pick and choose from the company's Marketplace store whichever parts of the new machine you wanted. If all you wanted was the beautiful new CNC aluminium chassis and input cover, go for it; if you just wanted the new touch…

title: The Pokémon Company is turning to facial recognition scans to help combat scalpers
summary: A high price to pay for your chase card.
body: Nintendo has announced the rollout of a facial recognition system and new entry and purchase rules for its Pokémon stores in Japan. It's not exactly a last-ditch effort, but it's yet another attempt at combating scalpers which have been plaguing the hobby ever since its inception. "In order to provide a safe and secure shopping environment for all customers, to prevent crime, and to ensure compliance with appropriate entry and purchase rules, we will be using a facial recognition system to verify the identity of customers," The Pokémon Company has explained in new guidance (via IGN ). The only exception to this will be Children under elementary school age, so preschoolers, up to six years old. (Image credit: The Pokémon Company) This is to help manage the one-time limit per day rule where people are only allowed to enter and purchase from a Pokémon store once a day to help ensure more players get access to stock. "If the system detects that the same person has entered the store more than once in one day or received more than one entry ticket, and a notification (alert) to that effect is displayed on the screen, entry will be denied to that person based on the system's judgement." …

body: Have you ever been sick of your family using your electronics without asking, and thought 'boy, I should put spikes and a taser on this thing'? That makes it tough to hold. From there, they rigged up a Raspberry Pi with a speaker to an object detection camera, and wrote a Python script to "play a goofy audio clip" and set off a taser fitted to the top of the Deck after a few seconds. No, they don't say what the audio is. As far as I can tell, the taser is just there to scare would-be battery thieves, as it can't make contact from its perch above the Steam Deck. title: PowerA LucidSound LS500/P review
summary: A potential slam dunk for budget headsets.
body: When most people are looking for a gaming headset they want it to have a few things: work with their platform of choice, sound good, decent mic, and a reasonable battery life. Other features like noise cancelling are nice but unnecessary, as well as adding to the price of the unit. The LucidSound LS500 does away with such frivolities and focuses in on what you really need in a headset, delivering a surprisingly good pair of cans for under $70 USD. Taking the headset out of the box the first thing I noticed is how light it is. The LucidSound LS500 boasts long haul battery life of up to 70 hours, so I was expecting a heavier fit. Instead it is a lightweight and comfortable headset. This is thanks to the plastic construction, which feels a little cheap but makes up for it in featherweight comfort. It even includes glasses slots to make long wear for four-eyed folks like me. It’s not as comfortable as Turtle Beach’s solution but does a far better job than the likes of top dog Razer BlackShark’s for glasses comfort. Despite this, they are living up to their battery life quotas as I have yet to charge this headset after many tens-of-hours of testing. This lightweight plastic constructio…

body: I am actually really excited for Zach Cregger's upcoming Resident Evil film . I think this may be the best chance there is for getting an actually good adaptation, mostly thanks to the fact that Cregger seems like a super fan who actually understands what makes the games so charming. In other words: he knows ball . "I want fans of the games to just know that I am a giant fan of the games, I am making this movie to celebrate the games—I haven't seen the other movies," Cregger said during an interview with ScreenRant . "What I'm not doing in this is that I'm not going to cannibalise the characters and the stories that the games already do so well, because I'm not going to be able to improve on Leon. (Image credit: Sony Pictures Entertainment) "I feel like what I'd rather do is tell an original story that lives in the world of the games, that obeys the rules of the games largely, but feels like more of the experience you get when you're playing the games. title: Yet Another Zombie Defense HD, which is its real name, is free on Steam for a limited time
summary: Load up on guns, bring your friends.
body: The era when it seemed like every second game was about zombies and the one where I played a lot of Flash games because they were free had a lot of overlap. Which is why I have fond memories of the hours I lost playing games like The Last Stand and Rebuild 2. I've just had a flashback to that time thanks to Yet Another Zombie Defense HD, which has had its price temporarily dropped by 100%. It's a twin-stick shooter where you spend the nights shooting zombies and the days building defenses, erecting barricades and saving up to buy a turret and then realizing you also need to buy a gun to mount on top of that turret. There's local and online multiplayer, a bunch of weapons and traps to unlock and modes to play, and it sure does have the look and feel of an indie game from a bygone age—even if it was only released in 2017. It's got a Steam Workshop too , where you can download skins to make your survivor look like Hatsune Miku, Garfield, Deadpool, or Shrek. Never change, Steam Workshop. Yet Another Zombie Defense is available for free to promote the upcoming release of Yet Another Zombie Survivors , which is a bullet heaven game with the same aesthetic and an escalating horde that bu…

title: One of the best shooters around just got a barely recognizable second episode, and it's only $12
summary: I love checking in on a New Blood game and seeing it completely transform in early access.
body: New Blood's comic book golden age noir detective immersive sim shooter, Fallen Aces, just got a beefy new update: Its second episode, Shadow of Death , is playable right now, while the usually $15 game is on sale for $12 until August 8. I'm kind of allergic to playing games in early access, so I haven't touched Fallen Aces since I fell in love with its first few levels back in 2024. Those levels were fun, the stealth tense, the combat beautifully slapstick, and the pulpy story engaging. But I mean it as a compliment when I say that the Episode 2 trailer shows a practically unrecognizable game. It's got car chases, sprawling city environments, medieval broadswords, and I lost track of how many new guns. Shout out to the cartoony Mateba Model 6 Unica in there, a.k.a the cyberpunk detective gun. The more games that sport this beautiful Italian oddity, the better. New Blood's entire main lineup of the 2020s has been slow to cook, but the three games have justified that time with ambitious increases of scope. title: Capcom wants to release a Resident Evil every year and sees remakes as the way to make it happen
summary: It's worked well so far.
body: As part of an interview in the latest issue of GameInformer (spotted via GamesRadar ), Capcom producer Masachika Kawata outlined the resurgent Japanese publisher's approach to Resident Evil: Quality and quantity, with remakes bolstering the process and helping fund the development of more adventurous projects. According to Kawata, Capcom would like Resident Evil to be a fully annual franchise, but "producing a new entry in the Resident Evil series every year would be quite an undertaking and a difficult task." That's where the remakes come in. "Being able to revisit older games and remake them helps Capcom meet that goal of releasing a Resident Evil title each year, but it also allows the team to continually challenge themselves and hone their craft," said Kawata. "That's not to say the remakes are any less important. In fact, they're just as important as the mainline titles. "Capcom is lucky enough to have found this cycle that can continue to provide us with the financial resources to create things like new entries in the Resident Evil series and completely new IP like Pragmata. So there is that relationship there." Phrases like "every year" tend to get my dander up when it come…

title: The new 'backward compatible' Xbox games on PC run on an OG Xbox emulator inside an Xbox 360 emulator, and people have already used it to run other Xbox 360 games
summary: Emulator turducken.
body: First reported by Tom's Hardware , it's come to light that, not only are the four " Backward Compatibility on PC " original Xbox games released last week running on a double layer of Xbox console emulation, but savvy independent developers have already used those emulators to run other Xbox games on PC. Developer Nathan on X, "The Everything App," has a succinct topline explanation: "The new OG Xbox Backwards Compatibility layer released by Microsoft for the PC is actually an Xbox 360 emulator running XeFu (the OG Xbox emu for the 360)," he wrote, pointing to telltale indicators visible in a dump of XeFu (the Xeon Fusion Emulator) pulled from the Fuzion Frenzy PC re-release. By combining Microsoft's recently-released PC port of XeO3 with specific components of XWine1, SlimEra namely, it becomes possible to run dumped backwards-compatible Xbox 360 and Xbox Original games before they see an official PC release, with varying degrees of success pic.twitter.com/6eocCCT1cW July 23, 2026 For an even more in-depth explanation, developer Milenko has an article on the subject, also on X. title: Red Faction: Guerrilla Re-Mars-tered review (2018)
summary: Red Faction still has the best destruction in games ever.
body: From the archives: This story originally ran in PC Gamer #321 (UK, Sep. 2018). The review appears as originally written, with only minor changes in formatting and presentation. It’s a damn crime that no game ripped off Red Faction: Guerrilla’s Geo-mod destruction feature. You take a hammer and you use it to smash out a panel of a wall and break through a pillar. Smash out a few more walls and maybe the building creaks. A few more whacks of the hammer later and the whole thing comes down, perhaps with you inside. And hey, maybe it knocks through another building on the way down. It’s still amazing to watch. Guerrilla does this one thing really well. It’s an otherwise uninspired open world game, with okay driving, unimpressive shooting and a boring story. Hell, Mars doesn’t even look that nice, because it’s Mars. But knocking down buildings in an open world is more than enough to carry this game. You’ll crash a jeep through a base. You’ll detonate mines and blow up a bridge, which will then collapse on top of an enemy settlement. You’ll melt the beams of a tower and watch it fall over. title: Final Fantasy 14 is planning 2 major overhauls to its housing system to catch up with World of Warcraft: 'It's probably the number 1 thing on the list a lot of people are requesting'
summary: Secret housing changes are afoot.
body: I wasn't expecting Final Fantasy 14 director and producer Naoki Yoshida to directly call out World of Warcraft during a media Q&A at the MMO's Berlin Fan Festival, but that's exactly what happened. When asked about how the team plans to modernise Final Fantasy 14's housing system—one which is regularly criticised for a lack of supply to meet demand and a fairly obtuse UI to boot—Yoshida's first response was: "I get the feeling that what you really want to ask is, well WoW has come up with this amazing housing system. How about [Final Fantasy] 14?" Blizzard's own MMO has finally taken its first stab at player housing, and I do admit I've been looking on with some envy. It looks far easier to wield and far more customisable with freely scaling and placing objects, and that's something that Yoshida has absolutely taken notice of. "We have immense respect for the World of Warcraft team," Yoshida said. "So when we saw that the World of Warcraft team announced the new housing system—and they said specifically that they looked to 14 and incorporated things which they wanted to surpass us in—I think that in itself is a great honour for us to hear." (Image credit: Blizzard) Yoshida said th…

title: Final Fantasy 14 boss Yoshi-P doesn't get the deal with Chort
summary: Yoshi-P is not chortin' it.
body: Remember Chort? He's a sub-boss in one of Final Fantasy 14's newest dungeons—a magnificent large-and-in-charge lad who rolls up into a ball and charges around the arena like a giant, fleshy Sonic the Hedgehog. I couldn't stop laughing the first time I fought him, and I wasn't the only person to immediately fall in love with how ridiculous he was . He quickly became memed to hell and back—from his goofy name, to the real "Mom, I frew up" stance he's rocking as he patiently waits for you to enter the boss room and beat him up. (Image credit: Square Enix) His immense reception came as quite the surprise to director and producer Naoki Yoshida. "I'm really glad to hear that Chort was so well received, but honestly I couldn't really understand the appeal of Chort," he said during a press Q&A at the game's Berlin Fan Festival. title: 'The last time I liked everything about a game was probably Baldur's Gate 3': Raphael Colantonio, co-founder of Arkane Studios, talks us through the games installed on his PC
summary: Lovecraftian misadventures, cat-breeding tactics games and, of course, Thief.
body: Disk Cleanup (Image credit: Future) Welcome to Disk Cleanup , our regular weekend feature delving into the PCs of PC gaming luminaries. Come back every weekend to read a new interview, digging into the important questions, like "How tidy is your desktop?" and "What game will you never uninstall?" Raphaël Colantonio became a PC gamer for a very specific reason—he was a huge Ultima fan and wanted to play Ultima 7. "Number six did not come out on Apple. It was so painful to me, the idea I could not play Ultima, that I bought a PC," says the co-founder of Arkane Studios. "It ended up being exactly what I wanted, because it [had] way more possibilities than any of the Ultimas until then." After working at companies like EA and Infogrames, in 1999 Colantonio co-founded Arkane Studios. The studio's debut game was Arx Fatalis, a first-person RPG inspired by Looking Glass' genre-redefining Ultima Underworld . Over the next two decades, Arkane established itself as the modern successor to Looking Glass, developing some of the PC's best games, such as 2012's Dishonored and 2017's Prey . title: Rockstar co-founder says 'I don't know if I personally care' if games release on disc, adds 'I love physical media'
summary: "If people want that, I think companies should provide it."
body: I still remember the long ritual of installing World of Warcraft to my parents' laptop as a young'un, mystified by the sheer number of discs it took to squeeze the game onto a hard drive. The more discs a game took to install, the better it must be, I figured—child me would be aghast at the contemporary world, where game boxes come with mere codes inside and PlayStation is killing off disc production . That last factoid has triggered commentary all over the industry and beyond, with everyone from Ubisoft's Yves Guillemot and French politician Jean-Luc Mélenchon weighing in. Speaking to IGN , Rockstar co-founder Dan Houser gave his own commentary on the physical vs. digital debate with a multifaceted answer. "I don't know that I care. If people want that, I think companies should provide it," he said. "But I don't know that I personally care. And I also think the ability to update games, as critical as people are of digital releases, the ability to update and fix problems in games has been really useful for the quality of games." Notably, both physical and downloadable patches existed before digital distribution became the rule. Magazines like the superlative PC Gamer would even he…

title: A classic Giger-inspired adventure game just got a sequel
summary: Tormentum 2 is out now.
body: H. R. Giger's biomechanical nightmares have inspired plenty of videogames. If we go way back, his work was repurposed for baffling puzzle adventure Dark Seed , and more recently there was the fleshy horror of Scorn . Tormentum: Dark Sorrow was more in the vein of the former than the latter, a point-and-click adventure that took Giger's stylings (and those of Zdzisław Beksiński too) as inspiration for its hand-painted horrors. A full 11 years after its release, and after eight years of development, Tormentum finally has a sequel. Tormentum 2 is a standalone game though, just one in a similar style, which is to say that it's full of bones and alien faces and naked people who are embedded in walls. In Tormentum 2 you're trapped inside a simulated world that's got out of hand, the supposedly digital characters within suddenly out of control and talking about gods from distant places. You have to cross the islands that make up this world, solving puzzles as you go, and working your way toward one of multiple endings. title: A crossover between Dungeons & Dragons and World of Warcraft has leaked
summary: Seems likely to be more than just a starter set this time, as we've seen in previous crossovers like Stranger Things or Rick & Morty.
body: This year's Gen Con event is one Wizards of the Coast has said it's "pulling out all the stops for", with a keynote to be hosted by Theo Solomon (who played Wyll in Baldur's Gate 3) including a bunch of announcements about what's coming up for Dungeons & Dragons. One release seems to have been leaked early: a crossover with World of Warcraft. According to a news post on virtual tabletop Roll20 that has since been removed (you can find it on RPG site EN World ), we can expect Warcraft to get at least a setting book for D&D 5th edition, as a couple of Magic: The Gathering worlds have previously. This wouldn't be the first collaboration between Blizzard and D&D. Around the time of Diablo 2 there were several official books by Wizards of the Coast adapting the world of Sanctuary to D&D's rules. Later there was a World of Warcraft RPG using D&D's 3rd edition, though that was published under the terms of the Open Gaming Licence by White Wolf, the publisher responsible for Vampire: The Masquerade (which also has a D&D crossover in the works ).
